title: Horizon-Aware Early Event Prediction for Tokamak Disruption Alarms
abstract: arXiv:2609.24443v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reliable disruption prediction is essential for the safe operation of future tokamaks. Existing full-distribution survival methods model the complete residual time-to-disruption distribution, whereas operational decisions primarily depend on disruption risk within a finite prediction horizon. This mismatch motivates introducing Early Event Prediction (EEP) objectives into survival-based disruption prediction. We take Deep Survival Machines (DSM) as the full-distribution baseline and propose applying two established EEP methods to tokamak disruption prediction: Temporal Label Smoothing (TLS), which directly predicts disruption probability within a finite horizon, and survTLS, which additionally models the event-time distribution within that horizon. Using a common causal encoder, we compare these methods on DIII-D, Alcator C-Mod, and EAST. We distinguish threshold-free deadline ranking from validation-selected fixed-policy alarm perform

translated_title: 面向托卡马克破裂警报的视界感知早期事件预测
translated_abstract: 可靠的破裂预测对于未来托卡马克的安全运行至关重要。现有的全分布生存分析方法对完整的剩余破裂时间分布进行建模，而实际的运行决策主要依赖于有限预测视界内的破裂风险。这种不匹配促使我们将早期事件预测（EEP）目标引入基于生存分析的破裂预测中。我们以深度生存机（DSM）作为全分布基线，提出将两种已有的EEP方法应用于托卡马克破裂预测：其一是时间标签平滑（TLS），它直接预测有限视界内的破裂概率；其二是survTLS，它在此基础上还对视界内的事件时间分布进行建模。通过使用共同的因果编码器，我们在DIII-D、Alcator C-Mod和EAST装置上对上述方法进行了比较，并区分了无阈值的截止期限排序性能与通过验证集选择的固定策略警报性能。
tldr: 该论文针对全分布生存方法与运行决策中有限预测视界需求不匹配的问题，提出将早期事件预测（EEP）目标引入基于生存分析的托卡马克破裂预测，以深度生存机为基线应用TLS和survTLS两种方法在有限视界内直接预测破裂风险，并在DIII-D、Alcator C-Mod和EAST三个装置上进行了验证。
en_tdlr: This paper addresses the mismatch between full-distribution survival methods and finite prediction horizons in operational decisions by introducing Early Event Prediction (EEP) objectives into survival-based tokamak disruption prediction, applying TLS and survTLS with a Deep Survival Machines baseline, and validating on DIII-D, Alcator C-Mod, and EAST.
